verdicts.explanation: Confirmed by multiple outlets covering the AKASA/HFMA April 2025 survey: 80% of health systems said they are exploring, piloting, or implementing generative AI tools for revenue cycle management in 2025 (Fierce Healthcare: '80% of health systems say they're exploring, piloting or implementing gen AI tools for RCM in 2025'; HIT Consultant: '80% of health systems are currently taking action on GenAI tools for revenue cycle management—whether exploring, piloting, or fully implementing').

verdicts.quote: a 38% jump in under two years, up from ~58% merely *considering* it in 2023

Fierce Healthcare reports the 80% figure as 'a 38% jump in less than two years, compared to 58% of health systems in 2023 who were merely considering gen AI for the revenue cycle.' The 2023 baseline is corroborated by AKASA's own November 2023 press release on the earlier AKASA/HFMA survey (250+ CFOs and revenue cycle leaders), which found 'nearly 60 percent of respondents indicated they are actively considering these new technologies for their revenue cycle operations.' Note the 38% is a relative increase (58% → 80%), which is how the report phrases it.

verdicts.quote: Roughly 40% were already piloting or implementing.
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed by Fierce Healthcare's coverage of the AKASA/HFMA April 2025 survey: 'about 40% of health systems are either piloting or implementing gen AI tools in their operations, while another 39% are exploring their options.' (The survey also found this skews by size: 64% of large health systems vs ~20% of $500M–$1B systems were piloting/implementing.)

verdicts.quote: name a **pilot-success owner** (roughly doubles conversion)
verdicts.explanation: No authoritative source supports the specific statistic that naming a dedicated pilot-success owner roughly doubles pilot-to-paid conversion. Related but different findings exist — e.g., a 2023 Forrester study (cited by Monetizely) found enterprise pilots with predefined success criteria were 3.2x more likely to convert than open-ended evaluations, and SaaStr cites 60-90% paid-pilot-to-contract conversion in well-run enterprise sales — but nothing ties a 'roughly 2x' effect to designating a pilot-success owner. This appears to be a heuristic/rule-of-thumb, not a citable data point.

verdicts.quote: Cair Health, SuperDial \$15M, LunaBill, VoiceCare AI, Stedi \$142M
verdicts.explanation: All entities check out. Cair Health (founded 2023, San Francisco; ~$500K seed per Tracxn/Crunchbase) sells AI agents that automate medical insurance/claims workflows. LunaBill (YC Winter 2025) sells AI voice agents for healthcare billing teams (claim status, AR recovery, appeals follow-up). VoiceCare AI (launched Feb 2025 with a Mayo Clinic pilot; $4.54M seed led by Caduceus Capital Partners with Mayo Clinic participating) automates payer back-office calls (benefits verification, prior auth, claims). The dollar figures in the quote also verify: SuperDial raised a $15M Series A led by SignalFire (announced June 24, 2025), and Stedi's total funding is $142M as of its $50M Series C (March 2026). All started roughly 1-3 years before mid-2026.

verdicts.quote: Infinitus, Mandolin, Develop Health, Sohar, Assort, Thoughtful, SuperDial
verdicts.correction: Six of the seven are active competitors in eligibility/benefits-verification/prior-auth automation: Infinitus (voice AI agents for payer/PBM benefit-verification and prior-auth calls, 100M+ minutes), Mandolin ($40M raised June 2025; insurance verification, benefits checks, and prior auth for specialty/infusion drugs), Develop Health ($14.3M Series A; GenAI benefit verification incl. AI calls to PBMs and prior-auth submission), Sohar Health ($3.8M seed, March 2025; API-based real-time eligibility/VoB), Thoughtful AI (RCM agents incl. eligibility-verification agent EVA), and SuperDial ($15M Series A; voice AI for eligibility, prior-auth, and claim-status payer calls). verdicts.explanation: Verified each company. Infinitus, Mandolin, Develop Health, Sohar, Thoughtful, and SuperDial all confirmed in eligibility/prior-auth automation (a mix of payer phone calls, API checks, and portal automation). Assort Health is consistently described by Forbes, TechCrunch, Fierce Healthcare, and its own site as voice AI for patient calls (scheduling, cancellations, FAQs) — patient access, not payer-facing eligibility/prior-auth work.

verdicts.quote: Rising (SuperDial, VoiceCare AI; R1 Phare Flow)
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed: SuperDial's voice AI agents automate insurance claim follow-up / claim-status / denial follow-up calls (e.g., 10,000+ claim-status calls per month at West Coast Dental), and VoiceCare AI's agent 'Joy' automates payer communications including claims management and follow-up — so both compete in AR follow-up / denial-chasing call automation and the lane is genuinely crowding (Infinitus, LunaBill, and Prosper AI also operate there). One naming nit in the underlying quote: R1's platform is called 'Phare' / 'Phare OS' (launched October 2025, with modules like Phare Claim), not 'Phare Flow.'

verdicts.quote: CodaMetrix, Fathom, Nym, Arintra, Maverick
verdicts.explanation: All five are established autonomous medical coding vendors, tracked head-to-head by KLAS, AVIA Marketplace, and CB Insights: CodaMetrix (founded 2019, Boston; MGB spinout), Fathom (touchless ICD/CPT/E&M coding across specialties, up to 90% automation), Nym (founded 2018, NY; ED-focused engine, 95%+ accuracy), Arintra (GenAI EHR-integrated autonomous coding, 82%+ chart automation), and Maverick Medical AI (founded 2019; real-time autonomous coding, ~85% direct-to-bill, deployed at RadNet and partnered with Infinx/ImagineSoftware). The segment is demonstrably crowded — KLAS runs a dedicated autonomous-coding comparison category.

verdicts.quote: ambient entrants (Abridge, Ambience)
verdicts.explanation: Both ambient-documentation companies have moved into coding/revenue-cycle territory. Abridge markets an 'Ambient AI for Revenue Cycle' platform that surfaces ICD-10, HCC, and CPT codes in real time and auto-calculates E&M levels from ambiently generated notes. Ambience Healthcare ships AutoCDI plus real-time ICD-10/CPT/HCC coding embedded at the point of care, launched an AI ICD-10 coding assistant for inpatient care (Fierce Healthcare), and published results claiming its coding model outperforms board-certified physicians on ICD-10 accuracy by 27% (trained with OpenAI reinforcement fine-tuning).

verdicts.quote: Rivet, Aspirion ContractIQ, R1 underpayment recovery
verdicts.explanation: All three verified. Rivet Health sells payment-variance-detection / underpayment recovery software (Payer Performance product; contract modeling, underpayment workflows). Aspirion's ContractIQ is a real product — 'ContractIQ Payment Variance AI' extracts payer contract terms at scale and applies payer policies and CMS guidelines to identify payment variances/underpayments; its 2026 rollout is widely discussed in RCM trade coverage. R1 offers a named 'Underpayment Recovery' service line (AI plus contract-modeling experts; case study claiming 99.7% capture rate and $45M recovered over six years).

verdicts.quote: payer-side Machinify/Lyric/Apixio
verdicts.correction: Machinify and Lyric are distinct payer-side payment-integrity vendors, but Apixio should not be listed as a third independent player: Apixio's Payment Integrity business merged with The Rawlings Group and VARIS to form the combined company that rebranded as Machinify (merger completed and rebrand announced by early 2025) — i.e., 'Apixio payment integrity' and 'Machinify' are the same entity as of mid-2026. The remaining Apixio-branded business is a risk-adjustment / Connected Care platform, not a separate payment-integrity competitor. Corrected statement: 'payer-side Machinify (which absorbed Rawlings, Apixio Payment Integrity, and VARIS) and Lyric.'
verdicts.explanation: Machinify's own press release and Crunchbase confirm The Rawlings Group + Apixio Payment Integrity + VARIS merged into a single payment-accuracy platform now branded Machinify (KLAS 2025 First Look covers the merged entity). So the claim is directionally right — all three names operate payer-side in payment integrity — but by June 2026 the Machinify/Apixio-PI double-listing was already outdated.

verdicts.quote: Sonnet 4.6 workhorse, Opus 4.8 for hard reasoning, Haiku 4.5 for high-volume simple steps

All remain active in Anthropic's current model lineup as of July 2026. One freshness note (post-dating the June 2026 report): Claude Sonnet 5 launched June 30, 2026 with near-Opus-4.8 agentic performance at the same Sonnet price point ($2/$10 intro through Aug 31, 2026, then $3/$15), so a report updated today would likely name Sonnet 5 rather than Sonnet 4.6 as the workhorse — but the claim as written about the mid-2026 lineup is accurate.

verdicts.quote: # BAA + zero-retention terms on the PHI path
verdicts.explanation: Anthropic does offer both: (1) Business Associate Agreements for Claude API commercial customers — eligible organizations can execute the BAA and enable 'HIPAA-ready' processing of PHI directly from the Claude Console; and (2) zero-data-retention (ZDR) arrangements for Claude API customers, subject to Anthropic's approval. Two caveats worth knowing when implementing: HIPAA-readiness and ZDR are distinct arrangements (HIPAA-readiness applies encryption/access-control/audit safeguards rather than requiring immediate deletion), and certain 'Covered Models' (e.g., Claude Fable 5) require 30-day retention and are not available under ZDR; the BAA also excludes some surfaces (Workbench/Console, beta features). None of this contradicts the claim that BAA + zero-retention terms are available on the API PHI path.

verdicts.quote: roughly **2–3 years out** for organizations that invest now

The industry today operates between Levels 1-2.
verdicts.correction: A vendor executive (Innovaccer CEO Abhinav Shashank, quoted in TechTarget, Feb 23, 2026) projects Level 4 'systemic automation' as roughly 2-3 years out for organizations that invest now in a unified platform approach; analysts quoted alongside him are more skeptical (Chartis' Prashant Karamchandani: true autonomy may take over a decade).

The claim correctly frames these as vendor-reported numbers.

verdicts.quote: report **30–40% drops in denial rates** (athenahealth and others)

The '30-40% reduction in denials' figure appears only in third-party RCM/SEO blogs describing predictive-denial tools generally (e.g., iRCM, rcmexperts.us), not in athenahealth's official materials.
verdicts.correction: Predictive-denial and claim-scrubbing tools are credited with 30-40% denial reductions in third-party RCM industry write-ups, but athenahealth's own published results (as of June 2026) are a ~16% reduction in insurance-related denials, a 30% increase in recovered payments on coding-related denials, and a 5.3% median denial rate across athenaOne customers vs. a >10% industry average.

This remains the latest edition of the survey as of July 2026. Minor scope note: the 14% covers AI use in the claims process broadly, which encompasses denial management.

verdicts.quote: 70–73% of healthcare AI pilots fail to convert[190]
verdicts.explanation: Directionally right but the range and citation need fixing. The report's footnote [190] points to a Medium post by 'AIADOPTS' that (a) has been deleted (HTTP 410 Gone), (b) claimed 70% of 847 AI POCs at consulting firms failed to convert — not healthcare-specific — and (c) is not an authoritative source. The defensible healthcare-specific figure is ~70%: the Bessemer Venture Partners / Bain / AWS 'Healthcare AI Adoption Index' (April 15, 2025; 400+ healthcare leaders across payers, providers, pharma) found only 30% of completed POCs reach production (46% at large providers). The '73%' upper bound has no identifiable source. The stated causes are broadly right: Bessemer's top blockers are security concerns (50-61%), insufficient in-house AI expertise (41-52%), expensive system integrations (43-51%), and data readiness (39-47%) — not model accuracy — though 'in-house expertise' is a top cause the report's framing omits. Note other estimates run higher (IDC 2025: ~88% of AI pilots never reach production; secondary healthcare write-ups: ~80%).
verdicts.correction: Approximately 70% of healthcare AI pilots fail to reach production: the Bessemer Venture Partners/Bain/AWS Healthcare AI Adoption Index (April 2025, survey of 400+ healthcare leaders) found only 30% of completed POCs reach production (46% among large providers), with top blockers being security concerns (50-61%), insufficient in-house AI expertise (41-52%), expensive integrations (43-51%), and data readiness (39-47%) rather than model accuracy. The '73%' upper bound and the cited Medium source (deleted; a general consulting-POC analysis, not healthcare) should be dropped.

verdicts.quote: free pilots rarely convert; paid pilots convert 60–90%+
verdicts.explanation: The 60-90%+ figure is real but it is a general B2B SaaS benchmark, not a measured healthcare-AI statistic. Jason Lemkin (SaaStr) writes that paid-pilot-to-annual-contract conversions 'vary fairly widely from about 60% to over 90%,' with higher rates when the customer gets fully into production during the pilot and lower rates when significant business-process change is required. 'Free pilots rarely convert' is widely repeated enterprise-sales/VC wisdom (e.g., B2B pilot playbooks state free pilots rarely convert and signal low commitment), but it is anecdotal, and some sources report high free-pilot conversion in other enterprise contexts. No healthcare-AI-specific dataset supports either number; the Bessemer Healthcare AI Adoption Index contains no paid-vs-free pilot breakdown.
verdicts.correction: Per the SaaStr (Jason Lemkin) B2B SaaS benchmark, paid pilots convert to annual contracts at roughly 60% to over 90%, with conversion highest when the customer reaches full production during the pilot; the advice that free pilots rarely convert is common enterprise-sales wisdom rather than a measured healthcare-AI statistic, and no healthcare-AI-specific paid-vs-free conversion data exists.

verdicts.quote: NRR >110%, CAC payback <12 months

verdicts.quote: Infinx invested in Maverick AI (Aug 2025)

On August 13, 2025, Infinx announced a strategic investment in Maverick AI, an AI company specializing in real-time autonomous medical coding, to bring real-time autonomous coding to revenue cycle management (85%+ direct-to-bill rate, 95% coding accuracy cited in the release). verdicts.quote: in 2025, B2B AI raised roughly 4x consumer AI; AI took ~61% of all global VC; vertical AI ~40%+ of funding
verdicts.explanation: The 61% figure is solid: OECD (Feb 2026) reports AI firms captured 61% of global VC in 2025 ($258.7B of $427.1B). The other two components are shaky. 'B2B AI raised ~4x consumer AI' appears only in secondary aggregators and is classification-dependent: PitchBook's Q1 2026 consumer-AI note puts B2C AI-enabled startup funding at $89B in 2025 (inflated by OpenAI/xAI/Anthropic/Waymo megadeals it classifies as B2C), which against OECD's $258.7B total implies closer to ~2x. 'Vertical AI ~40%+ of funding' overstates the dollar share: Euclid Ventures, the leading vertical-AI tracker, reports vertical startups captured ~30% of capital deployed in 2025 (36% of dollars in Q2 2025) while taking 53-57% of deal volume — 40%+ holds only for deal count, not dollars.
verdicts.correction: In 2025, AI companies captured 61% of global VC ($258.7B of $427.1B, per OECD, Feb 2026). Vertical AI accounted for a majority of AI/vertical deal volume (~53-57%) but only ~30-36% of capital deployed (Euclid Ventures, 2025/Q2 2025). The claim that B2B AI raised ~4x consumer AI circulates in secondary aggregators and depends on how foundation-model megadeals are classified; PitchBook counted $89B to B2C AI-enabled startups in 2025, implying a B2B:consumer ratio closer to ~2x under its taxonomy.

verdicts.quote: **net revenue retention >110%** and **CAC payback under 12 months**
verdicts.explanation: No authoritative source states these as healthcare-AI-investor-specific benchmarks. The figures are directionally consistent with widely used general SaaS venture benchmarks — Bessemer's Scaling to $100 Million puts median NRR at ~115-125% and best-in-class CAC payback under 12 months for SMB-focused companies — but Bessemer treats sub-12-month payback as best-in-class (not the norm) for enterprise sales (under 18-24 months is the enterprise bar), and no published healthcare-AI-specific benchmark matching '>110% NRR and <12-month CAC payback' was found. Treat as a plausible characterization of investor expectations rather than a sourced fact.

verdicts.quote: seed ~\$3.1M at ~\$15M pre overall[180] (~\$18M pre and ~\$4.6M median round for *AI-specific* seed)

The report's framing 'Commure reports' is accurate: this is a company-reported metric, not independently audited.

verdicts.quote: Change Healthcare/Optum (enterprise, later)
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed. Optum (UnitedHealth Group) completed its ~$13 billion acquisition of Change Healthcare on October 3, 2022, so Change Healthcare is part of Optum. Change Healthcare operates one of the largest claims clearinghouses/payment networks in the U.S. (AHA called it 'the largest U.S. Health Care Payment System'), fitting the enterprise-grade characterization; Availity and Stedi were separately confirmed as alternative clearinghouses.

verdicts.quote: AWS Textract / open-source
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed. AWS's product page describes Textract as a machine-learning service that 'automatically extracts text, handwriting, layout elements, and data from scanned documents,' including forms and tables from PDFs and images, and explicitly lists healthcare use cases such as extracting data from 'insurance claims, and pre-authorization forms.' Textract is also on AWS's HIPAA-eligible services list, making it suitable for EOB and denial-letter processing.

verdicts.quote: Vapi / Retell (faster, but HIPAA add-on / pricing premium)
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed on all parts. Vapi's docs state 'HIPAA mode requires an Enterprise subscription or a separately purchased HIPAA add-on' and that Vapi requires a signed BAA before enabling it — literally a HIPAA add-on/premium. Retell offers BAAs only on its Enterprise plan (a pricing premium over pay-as-you-go). For the component stack: Twilio signs BAAs for HIPAA-eligible products (requires Security or Enterprise Edition), Deepgram provides a BAA to qualifying customers on request, and ElevenLabs offers BAAs/HIPAA-eligible configurations for enterprise customers with Zero Retention Mode — all BAA-coverable as claimed.

verdicts.quote: U.S.-hosted VDI** (Amazon WorkSpaces / Azure Virtual Desktop)
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed. Amazon WorkSpaces is a fully managed DaaS/VDI offering assessed under AWS compliance programs including HIPAA, and Azure Virtual Desktop is Microsoft's VDI service covered by Microsoft's HIPAA BAA. Both can be deployed in U.S. regions, and hosting the desktop (and PHI) in a U.S. region while offshore staff access it remotely is a standard, supported pattern for keeping PHI U.S.-resident.

verdicts.quote: Vanta / Drata**-style automation for SOC 2
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed. Vanta markets its SOC 2 product as getting companies 'ready for a SOC 2 audit in weeks instead of months' with automated evidence collection, and Drata's SOC 2 framework product centralizes evidence, automates control monitoring, and streamlines audit readiness for continuous compliance — both are the standard compliance-automation tools for accelerating SOC 2 Type II attestation.

verdicts.quote: the Change Healthcare lesson, §7.2
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed. The February 21, 2024 ransomware attack on Change Healthcare took its clearinghouse/payment systems offline for weeks, freezing claims submission and payments for providers nationwide — AHA survey results (March 15, 2024) documented significant disruption to hospital finances and patient care, and the impact was severe enough that CMS opened accelerated/advance payment programs on March 9, 2024. This is a well-documented demonstration of single-clearinghouse dependence halting provider cash flow.

verdicts.quote: Stedi sandbox, Vanta/Drata for SOC 2 evidence
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed by primary sources. Stedi's official documentation (stedi.com/docs/healthcare/test-mode) uses the exact terms 'sandbox accounts' and 'test mode': 'Test mode provides a separate test environment where you can realistically simulate transactions in your Stedi account without PHI/PII,' with free mock eligibility checks against predefined payers (Aetna, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, CMS) for development use. Vanta's SOC 2 product page confirms it automates SOC 2 evidence collection (400+ integrations that 'automatically pull compliance evidence,' hourly control monitoring). Drata's SOC 2 page confirms it 'connects directly to your tech stack... to automatically collect and map evidence to SOC 2 controls.' Minor nuance only: Stedi sandbox accounts are limited to test mode and cannot submit test claims (a production account is required for test claims via SFTP/API), but this does not affect the claim as written.

verdicts.quote: Clearinghouse (Stedi, then Availity)
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed. Stedi's documentation describes integrating 'with the Stedi clearinghouse' supporting 270/271 eligibility, 837 professional/institutional/dental claims, and 276/277 claim status in both JSON and X12 EDI — an API-first, developer-oriented healthcare clearinghouse with a free sandbox/test mode, consistent with early-stage/startup use. Availity's site confirms it operates a 'Clearinghouse & Trading Partner Network' with 'national-scale transaction processing and trusted connectivity across eligibility, claims, and payments,' ~3M connected providers, 95 payers connected directly, ~$4T in billed claims and 13B+ transactions annually, self-described as the nation's largest dual-sided real-time healthcare network — consistent with the 'later scale' framing. The startup-vs-scale sequencing is a reasonable characterization of the two vendors' positioning, not a factual error.

verdicts.quote: (Cautionary: Olive AI.)
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed. Olive AI, once a ~$4B-valuation healthcare automation/RCM unicorn, announced on Oct 31, 2023 that it was winding down operations and selling its remaining business lines — the clearinghouse/patient access business to Waystar and the prior-authorization business to Humata Health (Fierce Healthcare, Oct 31, 2023; Lincoln International advised the asset sale). It is the standard cautionary tale for RCM AI.

verdicts.quote: AKASA, Adonis, Infinitus, CodaMetrix, Fathom, Nym Health, Arintra, Amperos Health
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed for 13 of 14 names. Directly verified via company sites: Arintra (AI autonomous medical coding integrated with Epic/athena/Cerner), Amperos Health (agentic-AI end-to-end insurance revenue recovery), RapidClaims (autonomous AI agents for coding/risk adjustment/denials), CombineHealth (SF-based 'AI employees' for coding, claims, and denial management — end-to-end AI RCM consistent with early stage), and Maverick Medical AI (autonomous coding, 85% direct-to-bill, RadNet partnership, Infinx investment). AKASA, Adonis, Infinitus, CodaMetrix, Fathom, Nym Health, Candid Health, and Sift Healthcare are all well-documented AI-driven RCM companies. Caveat: 'Procode AI' could not be located via available search channels (search budget exhausted; search engines blocked fetches) — if it is a real seed-stage startup it is too obscure to confirm; worth double-checking the name.

verdicts.quote: Smarter Technologies (New Mountain)
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed. New Mountain Capital's own newsroom shows it formed Smarter Technologies (announced May 19, 2025) by combining SmarterDx, Thoughtful.ai, and Access Healthcare into an AI-driven RCM platform. Note: the company website is NOT smartertechnologies.com (that is an unrelated UK IoT firm). Commure's site confirms it is an enterprise platform spanning ambient AI plus end-to-end RCM (billing automation, denial management, autonomous coding; 150+ health systems, $25B+ annual claims). Abridge (Series E, June 2025, explicitly expanding ambient AI into revenue-cycle integrity) and Ambience Healthcare (coding/CDI-aware ambient AI, $243M raise July 2025) are likewise enterprise ambient-AI platforms converging on RCM.

verdicts.quote: Infinitus, SuperDial, VoiceCare AI, LunaBill (voice to billing teams), Assort Health, Hippocratic AI
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed, with one nuance. All named companies are voice/front-door healthcare AI players: Infinitus (AI phone calls to payers for benefits/prior auth), SuperDial (voice AI payer calls sold to billing teams, by SuperBill), VoiceCare AI (voice agents for healthcare back-office calls; Mayo Clinic work), Assort Health (AI voice agents for patient access/call centers), Hippocratic AI (patient-facing voice agents), Tennr (AI referral/fax 'front door' automation), Mandolin (AI agents for infusion access/benefit verification), Develop Health (AI benefit verification and prior auth for prescriptions). LunaBill's site confirms it sells to hospitals and billing/RCM firms with AI agents that place real phone calls to payers (IVR navigation, hold, claim follow-up) — though voice is one component of a broader claims-automation platform rather than a pure voice product.

verdicts.quote: Stedi (X12→JSON / AI clearinghouse), Sohar Health (eligibility API)
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed. Stedi's healthcare page confirms it is a clearinghouse offering API-first eligibility (270/271) and claims APIs supporting both JSON and X12, with connectivity to 3,400+ payers; its positioning is developer/API-first (it has also marketed AI-agent readiness, e.g. an MCP server, though the page itself emphasizes APIs over 'AI'). Sohar Health confirmed as an insurance eligibility/verification API (Discovery, Verification, Network Status, Cost Estimate; 5M+ verifications annually). Cair Health confirmed selling six named AI RCM agents (coding, claims, denials, eligibility, payer calls, EOB extraction) to billing companies, digital health startups, and specialty EMRs — matching 'billers/BPOs/EHRs'. SuperDial (SuperBill) and LunaBill both sell voice-based payer-calling tools to billing teams.

verdicts.quote: Cohere Health, Lyric, Machinify (New Mountain), Evolent
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed. Machinify's site shows it is an AI payment-integrity platform for health plans (85+ customers including 18 of the top 20 health plans, 270M covered lives), and New Mountain Capital's newsroom confirms it announced acquiring Machinify on Jan 10, 2025 and combining it with its healthcare payment-integrity platform (the Rawlings Group/Apixio/VARIS combination), with the combined company operating under the Machinify name. Cohere Health (AI prior-authorization for health plans such as Humana), Lyric (AI claims-editing/payment integrity, ClaimsXten heritage), and Evolent (payer-delegated specialty care/utilization management with AI) are all established payer-side vendors.

verdicts.quote: launch of Phare OS
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed. R1 RCM announced Phare on October 22, 2025, explicitly marketed as 'healthcare's first Revenue Operating System powered by enterprise-grade AI,' integrating across major EHRs, connecting to 1,000+ payers with visibility into ~670M annual patient encounters, launched alongside an exclusive partnership with Singing River Health System. Covered by Becker's Hospital Review and TechTarget on Oct 22, 2025; R1's newsroom carries Phare/R37/Revenue Operating System topics.

verdicts.quote: Waystar adds agentic AI (Jan 2026)
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed. Waystar announced new agentic AI capabilities on January 12, 2026, as an extension of its AltitudeAI platform and described as 'a meaningful milestone on the path toward the autonomous revenue cycle' (agentic workflows that act within workflows, execute defined tasks, and learn with minimal intervention; AltitudeAI credited with preventing $15.5B in denials in under a year). TechTarget covered it with exactly the framing attributed: new agentic AI capabilities as part of the journey to make the revenue cycle autonomous.

verdicts.quote: 50+ AI/automation use cases on the unified "Fusion" architecture (HIMSS 2026)
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed. At HIMSS 2026 (announcement dated March 9, 2026), FinThrive (Plano, TX) unveiled an expanded agentic AI-powered revenue cycle platform built on its unified 'Fusion' data architecture, showcasing on the order of 50 AI and automation use cases across the architecture for predictive, autonomous revenue-cycle operations. Coverage cites '50' use cases; the report's '50+' is within reasonable rounding of the announcement's framing.

verdicts.quote: 20+ generative/agentic AI solutions (July 2025)
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed. On July 14, 2025 (PR Newswire), Omega Healthcare announced an expanded collaboration with Microsoft to launch more than 20 generative and agentic AI solutions for revenue cycle management, built on Azure AI (Azure AI Foundry) integrated with Omega's proprietary Omega Digital Platform (ODP). Also covered by HIT Consultant and TechTarget's revenue cycle publication.

verdicts.quote: Voice agents report ~**10% data-accuracy gains** and ~**50% ROI** vs. manual calling (Infinitus
verdicts.explanation: Infinitus's own homepage (fetched July 2026) states, in its 'Real results. Lower cost. Infinite scale.' section: '50% typical ROI and 10% greater data accuracy delivered.' This matches the claim's figures and attribution to Infinitus.

verdicts.quote: 400% ROI for a top-10 pharma
verdicts.explanation: Infinitus's resources/customer-stories page includes the case study 'Top-10 pharma company transforms patient access approach,' which states the company 'cut benefit verification time by half and delivered a 400% ROI by implementing Infinitus AI agents for one of their large brands.'

verdicts.quote: (Twilio, Deepgram, Anthropic, ElevenLabs all sign BAAs)
verdicts.explanation: All four confirmed on primary sources. Twilio: customers handling PHI 'must execute a Business Associate Addendum (BAA)' (available on Security/Enterprise Edition accounts). Deepgram: 'To secure a BAA (Business Associate Agreement) with Deepgram, please contact us' on its trust/data-privacy-compliance docs. Anthropic: privacy center article 'Business Associate Agreements (BAA) for Commercial Customers' — 'Anthropic provides a BAA covering our HIPAA-ready services, such as use of our first-party API or Enterprise plans.' ElevenLabs: enterprise page — 'We sign BAAs with HIPAA compliant configurations for qualifying enterprises.' Note each attaches conditions (plan tier, HIPAA-eligible products, zero-retention mode, etc.), but the claim as written is accurate.

verdicts.quote: Anthropic launched **Claude for Healthcare** (Jan 2026; BAA, native CMS coverage data/ICD-10/PubMed, prior-auth)[114]
verdicts.explanation: Anthropic announced Claude for Healthcare on January 12, 2026, timed to the JPMorgan Healthcare Conference (multiple outlets: Yahoo/Reuters-syndicated piece dated Jan 11, 2026; CIOL and Mint dated Jan 12, 2026). Coverage and the live claude.com/solutions/healthcare page confirm connectors to the CMS Coverage Database, ICD-10, NPI Registry, and PubMed, prior-authorization/claims-appeal workflows, and 'HIPAA-ready products'; Anthropic's privacy center separately confirms it provides BAAs for its HIPAA-ready API and Enterprise services.

verdicts.quote: OpenAI launched **OpenAI for Healthcare**
verdicts.explanation: OpenAI did launch a healthcare offering in January 2026, but it is branded 'ChatGPT Health' — a dedicated health experience inside ChatGPT that connects medical records and wellness apps (Apple Health, MyFitnessPal) — launched around January 7-8, 2026, days before Anthropic's Claude for Healthcare announcement. No product or program branded 'OpenAI for Healthcare' exists; searches of news coverage and openai.com surfaced no such name.
verdicts.correction: In early January 2026 (announced ~Jan 7-8, 2026), OpenAI launched ChatGPT Health, a dedicated consumer health experience within ChatGPT that securely connects medical records and wellness apps and is explicitly 'not intended for diagnosis or treatment.' OpenAI has not launched an offering branded 'OpenAI for Healthcare.'

verdicts.quote: Microsoft (Dragon Copilot into RCM coding), AWS (HealthScribe), and Google (MedLM/Vertex)
verdicts.explanation: Two of three parts check out: Microsoft's Dragon Copilot product page advertises going 'beyond note-taking with accurate coding suggestions,' supporting the RCM-coding extension claim; AWS HealthScribe is a live, HIPAA-eligible AWS service. However, Google's MedLM was deprecated before the report was written: Google Cloud's documentation states 'MedLM is deprecated. Access to MedLM will no longer be available on or after September 29, 2025.' Citing MedLM as a current Google healthcare AI offering in June 2026 was already stale.
verdicts.correction: Microsoft is extending Dragon Copilot beyond documentation into coding (the product offers 'accurate coding suggestions'), and AWS offers HealthScribe (HIPAA-eligible clinical documentation service). Google, however, deprecated MedLM — access ended on/after September 29, 2025 — and its current healthcare AI stack is MedGemma (open health models) and Gemini models served via Vertex AI.

verdicts.quote: Cleveland Clinic, Johns Hopkins; runs the HFMA adoption survey
verdicts.explanation: Two of three elements verify: AKASA and Cleveland Clinic announced a strategic collaboration on April 29, 2025 and deepened it October 13, 2025 (AKASA press page), and AKASA commissions the generative-AI revenue-cycle adoption survey fielded through HFMA's Pulse Survey program (Dec 17, 2025 release; 519 CFOs and revenue cycle leaders surveyed in April 2025). But I found no evidence anywhere — AKASA's site, press releases, or news searches — that Johns Hopkins is an AKASA customer; AKASA's named customers include Cleveland Clinic, Methodist Health System, and Montage Health.
verdicts.correction: AKASA's flagship customer is Cleveland Clinic (strategic collaboration announced April 29, 2025; expanded October 13, 2025); publicly named customers also include Methodist Health System and Montage Health, but there is no public evidence Johns Hopkins is a customer. AKASA commissions (rather than 'runs') the generative-AI adoption survey, which is fielded through HFMA's Pulse Survey program (most recently 519 CFOs/RCM leaders surveyed April 2025, published December 17, 2025).

verdicts.quote: 4x revenue growth in 2025; net retention >130%
verdicts.explanation: Adonis's Series C announcement (March 25, 2026; $40M round, total funding >$95M) states the company 'achieved more than 4x revenue growth in 2025' with 'net retention above 130%.' A separate January 2026 press release ('Adonis Achieves Over 4x Revenue Growth...') confirms it 'closed 2025 with over 4x revenue growth.'

verdicts.quote: 100M+ call-minutes; knowledge graph from 4M+ calls; serves 44% of Fortune 50 healthcare
verdicts.explanation: These were earlier Infinitus milestones that the company has since superseded. As of July 2026, infinitus.ai's homepage cites '200M+ minutes of conversation automated' and '8M+ calls completed supporting 125,000+ providers,' and its about page cites '>200M minutes' and '6M+ calls automated to payors, patients, and providers.' The Fortune 50 figure remains current: '44% of the Fortune 50 supported' (healthcare companies within the Fortune 50), plus '8 out of 10 of the top pharmaceutical manufacturers.'
verdicts.correction: As of July 2026, Infinitus reports 200M+ minutes of conversation automated and 6-8M+ calls completed (supporting 125,000+ providers), up from the earlier 100M-minute/4M-call milestones; it supports 44% of the Fortune 50 (healthcare companies) and 8 of the top 10 pharmaceutical manufacturers.

verdicts.quote: Mass General Brigham spinout; 220+ hospitals (27 states, ~12% of U.S. NPR); 96%+ automation
verdicts.explanation: Most of this verifies: CodaMetrix 'began as an internal initiative at Mass General Brigham' (evolved from the Massachusetts General Physician Organization's billing office), and its June 23, 2025 press release confirms 220 hospitals across 27 states representing over $180 billion in net patient revenue — 'nearly 12% of the U.S. total' (its Feb 4, 2026 Best in KLAS release cites 30+ health systems across 27 states). But the '96%+ automation' figure is unsupported: across CodaMetrix's published case studies the highest automation rates are 92% (OHSU radiology; CU Medicine radiology), 88% (University of Miami radiology), and 85% (MGB radiology); company-level claims are 'cut manual coding by 70%' and 'reduce coding costs by more than 50%.' No 96% automation figure appears in its press releases, case studies, or homepage.
verdicts.correction: CodaMetrix began as an internal initiative at Mass General Brigham (spun out of the Massachusetts General Physician Organization's billing operation) and, per its June 23, 2025 release, serves 220 hospitals across 27 states representing $180B+ in net patient revenue (~12% of the U.S. total). Its highest published automation rates are ~92% (radiology coding at OHSU and CU Medicine), not 96%+; company-wide it claims a 70% reduction in manual coding.

verdicts.quote: Lyric (ex-ClaimsXten pre-pay editing, ~190M lives)
verdicts.explanation: Lyric's own homepage (fetched 2026-07-19) states "190m lives supported," along with "9 of the top 10 U.S. health plans" and "35 years of proven results." The ClaimsXten lineage is confirmed: TPG closed its $2.2B acquisition of the ClaimsXten claims-editing business from Change Healthcare/UnitedHealth in October 2022 (a divestiture condition of the Optum-Change deal), and ClaimsXten was rebranded as Lyric on April 24, 2023 (Business Wire: "ClaimsXten Becomes Lyric, Welcomes Raj Ronanki as Chief Executive Officer"; also covered by HIT Consultant and Fierce Healthcare). A customer testimonial on lyric.ai explicitly references "ClaimsXten and Lyric's secondary claim editing expertise."

verdicts.quote: connections to over 95% of U.S. payers; 2,700+ payers and 3.4M+ providers
verdicts.explanation: The "largest network" and "95%" parts check out: Availity brands itself "the nation's largest real-time health information network" and its current site shows "95%" direct payer connectivity; its March 2025 press-release boilerplate says "connections to more than 95% of payers, more than 3 million providers and more than 2,000 trading partners." But the two specific counts are off: (a) Availity's own materials say "more than 3 million" (site tile: "3M") connected providers — the "3.4 million" figure appears in Availity's March 6, 2025 PR only as "Availity Essentials Pro serves over 3.4 million providers," i.e., a product-level figure, not the network stat; (b) I could not find "2,700+ payers" in any current or recent Availity material (site, about page, PR boilerplate) — the closest published figures are ">95% of payers" and "more than 2,000 trading partners" (site now says 17K connected B2B partners). Availity also cites over 13 billion transactions and ~$4T in billed claims annually.
verdicts.correction: Availity describes itself as the nation's largest real-time health information network, with direct connections to more than 95% of U.S. payers, more than 3 million connected providers, and over 13 billion clinical, administrative, and financial transactions annually (~$4T in billed claims) — per availity.com and Availity's March 2025 press boilerplate (as of July 2026). The "3.4 million providers" figure refers specifically to providers served by Availity Essentials Pro; drop or re-source the "2,700+ payers" count, which does not appear in Availity's published materials.

verdicts.quote: processes on the order of **15 billion transactions/year** (~\$1.5 trillion+ in claims)
verdicts.explanation: The 15-billion figure is the standard government/industry citation: HHS's March 5, 2024 statement on the cyberattack says Change Healthcare "processes 15 billion health care transactions annually," a figure also used by AHA and CRS. Change's own SEC prospectus (June 2019) said it facilitated "nearly 14 billion healthcare transactions and approximately $1 trillion in adjudicated claims or approximately one-third of all U.S. healthcare expenditures" (FY2018), and KFF Health News (March 2024) reported it "processes 14 billion transactions annually." The DOJ's February 2022 antitrust complaint put the value of claims flowing through Change's clearinghouse at more than $1.5 trillion per year. "On the order of 15 billion (~$1.5T+)" is consistent with these authoritative figures.

verdicts.quote: touching roughly one in three U.S. patient records
verdicts.explanation: Multiple independent anchors: Change Healthcare's own SEC prospectus said its network "transacts clinical records for over 112 million unique patients, more than one-third of the estimated total U.S. population"; The HIPAA Journal notes Change "states on its website that its systems touch the data of one in three Americans"; and the 1-in-3 patient-records figure was repeated by HHS and AHA throughout the 2024 attack response. (The eventual breach notification actually covered ~190-192.7 million people — more than half the US population — so "one in three" is, if anything, conservative.)

verdicts.quote: **February 2024 Change Healthcare cyberattack**
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed. Attackers (ALPHV/BlackCat) first accessed Change Healthcare systems on February 12, 2024, and deployed ransomware on February 21, 2024; UnitedHealth Group disclosed the incident in an SEC 8-K on February 22, 2024. The outage crippled the clearinghouse layer for weeks and ultimately exposed data of ~190 million people — consistent with the report's framing that it exposed the fragility of the clearinghouse layer.

verdicts.quote: X12→JSON for 3,400+ payers[126]
verdicts.explanation: Stedi's healthcare page (fetched 2026-07-19) states "Connect to over 3,400+ payers. We cover virtually all U.S. medical and dental payers" and "We support both JSON and X12," with its Eligibility Check and Claims APIs translating JSON to HIPAA-compliant X12 EDI (270/271, 837, 835). Its payer-network page currently lists 3,676 total payers, so "3,400+" remains accurate (Stedi's own marketing still uses 3,400+).

verdicts.quote: REST APIs via Optum developer portal
verdicts.explanation: developer.optum.com exists and offers the legacy Change Healthcare API families — e.g., an "Eligibility and Claims" section and "Optum Real for Medical" for real-time eligibility/claims/payment exchange — with sandbox access requests via the marketplace. No public pricing is posted; access and pricing run through Optum sales, consistent with "enterprise/negotiated non-public pricing."

verdicts.quote: **Epic, Oracle Health (Cerner), eClinicalWorks, NextGen, athenahealth, Veradigm, and MEDITECH**
verdicts.explanation: Uncontroversial list of the major US EHR/PM vendors. Definitive Healthcare's inpatient EHR market-share data shows Epic (43.9%), Oracle Cerner (18.9%), and MEDITECH (10.7%) controlling ~73% of the US hospital market, and eClinicalWorks, athenahealth, NextGen, and Veradigm (formerly Allscripts) are the standard leading ambulatory EHR/PM vendors in KLAS/Definitive rankings.

verdicts.quote: historically "App Orchard," rebranded in 2024 as **Epic Showroom**
verdicts.explanation: The lineage is right but the date is off. Epic retired the App Orchard branding in late 2022, restructuring vendor listings into Connection Hub and Toolbox under its vendor-services program (Fierce Healthcare, Dec 19, 2022: "Epic plans to overhaul its app market, opens new Connection Hub for developers"). Epic then unveiled "Showroom" at its August 2023 UGM (Fierce Healthcare, Aug 23, 2023: "Epic unveils new app 'showroom' for 3rd-party vendors") and launched the standalone showroom.epic.com marketplace website in January 2024 (Fierce Healthcare, Jan 18, 2024: "Epic launches new 'Showroom' website for 3rd-party apps, services"). So 2024 was only the website launch, not the App Orchard rebrand.
verdicts.correction: Epic retired the "App Orchard" branding in late 2022 (splitting listings into Connection Hub and Toolbox); it announced the successor marketplace "Showroom" at UGM in August 2023 and launched the standalone showroom.epic.com site in January 2024.

verdicts.quote: organized into Connection Hub for data integrations, Toolbox for clinical/workflow apps, and Workshop
verdicts.explanation: This describes Showroom's 2024–2025 structure. Workshop did exist — launched in early 2024 as Showroom's deepest co-development tier (initial categories: Ambient Voice with Abridge/Nuance, Contact Center with Talkdesk/Genesys, Patient Feedback with Press Ganey/Qualtrics) — but Epic quietly retired it around October 2025, folding its categories into Toolbox (Health API Guy, "The Quiet Burial of Epic's Workshop," Jan 2026). As of July 2026, Epic Showroom's own application code enumerates exactly two listing programs — ConnectionHub and Toolbox — with no Workshop; Toolbox listings are organized around Epic-defined "Blueprints," and Connection Hub remains the self-reported integration directory.
verdicts.correction: Epic Showroom is now (as of late 2025/2026) organized into Connection Hub (self-reported listings of live third-party integrations) and Toolbox (validated integrations built to Epic-defined Blueprints). Workshop, the co-development tier introduced in early 2024, was quietly retired around October 2025 and its categories were merged into Toolbox.

verdicts.quote: the ambulatory marketplaces (athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, Veradigm) matter more than Epic
verdicts.explanation: Three of the four named vendors verifiably operate branded ambulatory app marketplaces: athenahealth Marketplace (described by athenahealth as its 'app store' with 300-400+ integrated partner solutions), NextGen Healthcare's API Marketplace at nextgen.com/solutions/marketplace ('third-party vendor marketplace offering applications that use NextGen Healthcare APIs'), and Veradigm Connect with its App Expo ('hundreds of certified applications and devices for provider practices built on open APIs'). However, eClinicalWorks does not operate a comparable branded third-party app marketplace — multiple searches found only a partner program (eclinicalworks.com/about-us/partners) and FHIR/API interoperability endpoints, with no 'eClinicalWorks Marketplace' app store.
verdicts.correction: As of July 2026, athenahealth (Marketplace), NextGen Healthcare (API Marketplace), and Veradigm (Veradigm Connect / App Expo) operate ambulatory third-party app marketplaces; eClinicalWorks does not run a branded app marketplace and instead offers a partner program and FHIR/API-based integrations, so it should be characterized as an integration/partner channel rather than a 'marketplace.'

verdicts.quote: an aggregator (e.g., Redox) buys multi-EHR reach faster
verdicts.explanation: Redox (redoxengine.com) describes itself as a healthcare data integration platform that 'makes it easy to move clinical and administrative data from source systems into your preferred cloud environments' — i.e., an integration layer connecting digital-health products to many EHRs through a single API, sold as an ongoing subscription/managed service. Characterizing it as an aggregator that buys multi-EHR reach for an ongoing cost is accurate.

verdicts.quote: Epic's Showroom is a later, enterprise-credibility move
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed as of mid-2026: showroom.epic.com is live as Epic's public marketplace/product directory, and Epic's own Vendor Services site states 'Showroom helps you discover services and products for use with Epic.' Showroom (with Connection Hub as its entry-tier listing level) replaced the retired App Orchard brand (launched 2016), alongside Epic Vendor Services as the paid developer program. The name 'Showroom' is current.

verdicts.quote: RevGenius, HFMA chapters, senior AAPC/AHIMA members, ex-RCM-BPO ops leaders
verdicts.explanation: RevGenius is not a healthcare revenue-cycle community. Its own site describes a ~60,000-member community of 'revenue creators' — sales, marketing, and revenue operations professionals at fast-growing tech companies (Salesforce, HubSpot, OpenAI, etc.). The 'rev' is B2B SaaS go-to-market revenue, not healthcare revenue cycle management, so it is not a channel for recruiting U.S.-experienced RCM operators. The other named channels are valid: HFMA (Healthcare Financial Management Association) has local chapters of provider finance/revenue-cycle professionals, and AAPC/AHIMA are the medical coding/HIM credentialing bodies whose member networks contain experienced RCM staff.
verdicts.correction: Replace RevGenius with an actual RCM community: e.g., 'AAHAM (American Association of Healthcare Administrative Management) or HBMA (Healthcare Business Management Association) chapters, HFMA chapters, senior AAPC/AHIMA members, ex-RCM-BPO ops leaders.' RevGenius is a B2B tech sales/marketing/RevOps community, not an RCM talent pool.

verdicts.quote: (Availity, Change Healthcare, Waystar)
verdicts.explanation: All three are healthcare clearinghouses/claims networks. Availity calls itself 'the nation's largest dual-sided, real-time healthcare network,' processing 13B+ clinical, administrative, and financial transactions annually (eligibility, authorizations, claims, payments) across 95+ payers and 3M+ providers. Change Healthcare (an Optum subsidiary since Oct 2022) operates one of the largest claims clearinghouses — the February 2024 ransomware attack on it disrupted claims processing industry-wide, affecting ~190M people. Waystar (formed from Navicure + ZirMed) is an RCM/payments platform whose core includes claims clearinghouse functions (claim management/monitoring, eligibility, remittance, with a published payer list).

verdicts.quote: coder certification bodies (CPC/CIC/COC; CCS/CCA/CDIP)
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed on both organizations' certification pages. AAPC issues the CPC (Certified Professional Coder), CIC (Certified Inpatient Coder), and COC (Certified Outpatient Coder) credentials. AHIMA issues the CCS (Certified Coding Specialist), CCA (Certified Coding Associate), and CDIP (Certified Documentation Integrity Practitioner) credentials, among others (CCS-P, RHIT, RHIA, CHDA, CHPS).

verdicts.quote: R1 RCM (Phare OS)
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed via R1's own site and trade press. R1 launched 'Phare,' billed as 'healthcare's first Revenue Operating System powered by enterprise-grade AI,' on October 22, 2025, with three flagship products: Phare Access (patient access/intake), Phare Claim (autonomous coding and claim-error detection, up to 97% coding accuracy for ED/physician office visits), and Phare Flow (AI-agent claim follow-up/denials). R1 maintains a 'Phare OS' product page (r1rcm.com/enterprise-partnerships/phare-os: 'Phare OS unifies intelligence, automation and real-time visibility across the full revenue cycle'), and in June 2026 announced Payer Atlas and Phare Intelligence additions to Phare OS. The attribution is accurate as of mid-2026.

verdicts.quote: Optum/Optum360 (UnitedHealth; owns Change Healthcare)
verdicts.explanation: Optum is UnitedHealth Group's health-services segment, and Optum360 is its revenue cycle management subsidiary/brand (still in active use as of 2025-2026, e.g., optum360.com and Optum coding/RCM products). UnitedHealth Group's Optum completed the acquisition of Change Healthcare on October 3, 2022 in a deal valued at about $13 billion including assumed debt, folding it into Optum Insight; Change Healthcare remains an Optum subsidiary as of mid-2026.

verdicts.quote: Oracle Health (Cerner)
verdicts.explanation: Oracle announced its acquisition of Cerner in December 2021 and closed it in June 2022 (~$28.3 billion); the business was subsequently rebranded Oracle Health, headquartered in North Kansas City, MO. The surrounding list is also accurate — R1, FinThrive, Cognizant, Conifer Health, Ensemble Health Partners, Guidehouse, Experian Health, athenahealth, Veradigm, TruBridge, CareCloud, Huron, and Infinx are all real, active RCM/EHR/consulting incumbents in the US healthcare revenue-cycle market.

verdicts.quote: Sagility, GeBBS, CorroHealth, Coronis (Visionary RCM), Medusind, Vee Healthtek
verdicts.explanation: The parenthetical affiliation is factually wrong: Visionary RCM (Chennai, India; risk adjustment and RCM services, founded 2006) was acquired from The Carlyle Group on September 30, 2020 and became part of CorroHealth — not Coronis. CorroHealth was formed by combining its domestic middle-revenue-cycle group with Visionary RCM's global delivery model (plus T-System and RevCycle+). Coronis Health is a separate company: Veritas Capital acquired it from 424 Capital and completed its combination with MiraMed Global Services on August 4, 2022, which is what gives Coronis its India/global delivery. Additionally, 'India-based' is loose: most of these firms are US-headquartered with India-centric delivery (Omega Healthcare: Boca Raton, FL, with delivery in India/Philippines/Colombia; GeBBS: Los Angeles-area HQ with 16 global delivery centers; CorroHealth: Plano, TX; Medusind: Miami, FL; Vee Healthtek: US HQ with Bangalore delivery), while Sagility's listed parent, Sagility India Ltd, is Bengaluru-based (NSE/BSE-listed since November 2024).
verdicts.correction: The parenthetical should attach Visionary RCM to CorroHealth, not Coronis: 'Sagility, GeBBS, CorroHealth (which absorbed Chennai-based Visionary RCM in September 2020), Coronis Health (whose India/global delivery came via its August 2022 merger with MiraMed Global Services), Medusind, Vee Healthtek.' These are better described as India-centric RCM BPOs — mostly US-headquartered (Omega: Boca Raton FL; GeBBS: Los Angeles; CorroHealth: Plano TX; Medusind: Miami FL) with majority-India delivery workforces; Sagility India Ltd (Bengaluru) is the India-listed exception.

verdicts.quote: first autonomous coding in Epic Toolbox; #1 Best in KLAS 2026
verdicts.explanation: Both halves fail. (1) KLAS: CodaMetrix, not Fathom, was named No. 1 in the inaugural 2026 Best in KLAS category for Autonomous Coding (CodaMetrix press release, Feb 4, 2026; codametrix.com homepage banner says '2026 Rated #1 Best in KLAS'). Fathom's own site claims only '#1 solution for reducing cost of care' in the 2025 KLAS Emerging Solutions Top 20 report and 'highest overall score' in an earlier KLAS autonomous coding market segment report — not Best in KLAS 2026. So line 684 of the report is right and line 756 is wrong. (2) Epic Toolbox: Fathom was not first. Epic's Fully Autonomous Coding Toolbox category went live Aug 16, 2024, and at least three vendors received the designation on that same date — Fathom ('as of Aug. 16' per its Sept 12, 2024 announcement), CodaMetrix (press release dated Aug 16, 2024), and Nym (press release dated Aug 16, 2024). Neither Fathom's press release nor its website claims to be 'first'.
verdicts.correction: CodaMetrix was named No. 1 in the inaugural 2026 Best in KLAS: Autonomous Coding category (announced Feb 4, 2026). Fathom's KLAS distinctions are different: highest overall score in KLAS's autonomous coding market segment report and #1 for reducing cost of care in the 2025 KLAS Emerging Solutions Top 20. On Epic: Fathom, CodaMetrix, and Nym all received Epic Toolbox designation in the Fully Autonomous Coding category effective the same date, Aug 16, 2024, when the category launched — no vendor can accurately be called 'first.'

verdicts.quote: 96% accuracy; 250+ facilities
verdicts.explanation: Nym's own materials consistently state 'over 95%' accuracy, not 96%: homepage (July 2026) says it 'consistently maintain[s] over 95 percent coding accuracy'; its Aug 16, 2024 Epic Toolbox release, Oct 2024 $47M PSG investment release, Sept 18, 2025 TIME release, and Apr 21, 2026 CEO announcement all say 'over 95%' / 'over 95 percent accuracy'. On scale, current company materials cite '30+ health systems & physician groups' (homepage) and 'hundreds of healthcare facilities nationwide' (Apr 21, 2026 press release); a specific '250+ facilities' figure could not be found in Nym's current press releases or website.
verdicts.correction: Nym reports coding accuracy of over 95% (not 96%) with zero human intervention, and says it processes millions of charts annually for 'hundreds of healthcare facilities nationwide' (Apr 21, 2026 press release); its homepage cites 30+ health systems and physician groups as of July 2026.

verdicts.quote: 3,000+ locations; ~\$700M/yr recovered across 500K+ claims
verdicts.explanation: The numbers are confirmed by Amperos Health's Series A press release (Apr 22, 2026, $16M led by Bessemer Venture Partners): 'over 3,000 clinical locations across all 50 states,' 'nearly $700 million of revenue recovered per year,' and 'over 500,000 claims' (the homepage also cites 500K+ claims processed). However, the report's attribution of the AI agent name 'Doris' is wrong — Amperos's AI biller is named 'Amanda' ('Meet Amanda: the world's first AI biller for denials and collections,' Amperos blog, June 4, 2025). No 'Doris' product exists at Amperos.
verdicts.correction: Amperos Health (AI denial management/collections; its AI biller is named 'Amanda,' not 'Doris') serves over 3,000 clinical locations across all 50 states, recovers nearly $700M of revenue per year, and has worked over 500,000 claims, per its $16M Series A announcement led by Bessemer Venture Partners on April 22, 2026.

verdicts.quote: 150M+ patient interactions
verdicts.explanation: Assort Health's current figure is higher: its June 24, 2026 Series C announcement ($120M at a $1.2B valuation, total raised $222M+) cites a proprietary dataset of 190 million patient interactions, and its website (July 2026) says its platform is 'trained on 190M+ interactions across 23+ specialties.' The 150M+ figure was plausibly what the company published when the report was written in early June 2026, but it has since been superseded.
verdicts.correction: Assort Health's platform is trained on 190M+ patient interactions (per its June 24, 2026 Series C announcement of $120M at a $1.2B valuation, and its website as of July 2026).

verdicts.quote: ~\$764K ARR by early 2026, 50K+ calls; partners incl. Mayo, Experian Health
verdicts.explanation: LunaBill's Y Combinator profile (Fall 2025 batch) confirms the core facts but with important nuance: the $764K figure is 'contracted ARR,' of which only $428K is live — the report's '~$764K ARR' overstates live revenue. The YC page confirms partnerships 'with top healthcare leaders like UC health systems, Mayo, Experian Health and more.' Calls: the YC page now says 'automated 60,000+ insurance calls' (the 50K+ figure was plausibly accurate when written); LunaBill's own site (July 2026) reports 90,000+ payer interactions/month portfolio-wide and names customers Nutex Health, GeBBS, PharmBills, and UnisLink.
verdicts.correction: LunaBill (YC Fall 2025) reached $764K in contracted ARR ($428K live) with 60,000+ insurance calls automated per its YC profile; partners include UC health systems, Mayo, and Experian Health. As of July 2026 its website reports 90,000+ payer interactions per month portfolio-wide.

verdicts.quote: 500+ orgs, 130+ large systems (HCA, Tenet); reports 85%+ autonomous RCM
verdicts.explanation: All figures match Commure's own May 19, 2026 press release ($70M raise at $7B valuation): 500+ healthcare organizations served, 130+ major health systems, HCA Healthcare and Tenet Healthcare as named customers, and an 85%+ RCM autonomous completion rate (plus 3,000+ sites of care and tens of billions of dollars in annual claims). The homepage separately lists '130+ Health Systems' and names HCA Healthcare and Tenet Health among customers. Note these are company-reported figures; the report correctly hedges the 85% with 'reports'.

verdicts.quote: often routed through **Censinet** (the dominant health-system TPRM exchange)
verdicts.explanation: Supported, with the caveat that the evidence is largely company-reported. Censinet's Feb 23, 2026 press-release boilerplate describes it as 'the leading provider of healthcare cybersecurity risk management solutions' operating 'the industry's first and only cloud-based risk exchange,' serving 'more than 1,000 healthcare organizations with a network of over 50,000 vendors'; its about page cites a collaborative risk network of 'more than 55,000 vendors and products.' No comparable healthcare-specific TPRM exchange/network operates at that scale (competitors like CORL or HITRUST are assessment services/frameworks, not shared exchanges), so 'dominant health-system TPRM exchange' is a fair characterization, though no independent market-share data verifies 'dominant.'

verdicts.quote: reported a 10x increase in claims-followed-up-per-biller in week one and 100% pilot-to-paid conversion
verdicts.explanation: This matches LunaBill's Y Combinator company profile verbatim: 'Our customers see a 10x increase in claims followed up per biller in the first week' and 'we have converted 100% of pilots to paying customers.' Third-party aggregators of the YC profile repeat both metrics. These are company-reported claims, which the report accurately frames as 'reported.'

verdicts.quote: SuperDial and Cair Health already do this for payer calls and RCM agents respectively
verdicts.explanation: SuperDial (superdial.com, formerly SuperBill) is an AI platform that automates outbound healthcare phone calls to insurance payers (eligibility, prior auth, claim status, credentialing) and is positioned as 'built specifically for Revenue Cycle Management organizations,' selling to RCM companies, health systems, practices, and facilities. Cair Health sells AI agents for RCM (named agents for coding, claims, denials, eligibility, payer calls, and payment posting) to billing companies, digital health startups, and specialty EMR providers. Both are technology vendors to the RCM industry rather than RCM service operators, matching the report's characterization.

verdicts.quote: AGS's 500+ agents
verdicts.explanation: AGS Health's own AI Agents and Intelligent Automation page states: 'AGS Health has developed and operates over 500 digital agents in various RCM applications' (with examples: authorization agents doing 50% of production at 90-95% accuracy, a denials agent with a 98.1% automated success rate recovering $18M+ annually, and 10K+ automated appeals/month). verdicts.explanation: Waystar published "Waystar Introduces Agentic AI to Advance Toward the Autonomous Revenue Cycle" on January 12, 2026 (confirmed on Waystar's newsroom). The ~$100B figure is Waystar's own framing of the opportunity: in its Q1 2026 earnings materials and coverage (Fierce Healthcare, Apr 30, 2026) Waystar says its agentic strategy targets "approximately $100 billion in annual revenue cycle labor services performed across the industry," and its Q1 2026 investor slides cite a "$100 billion manual RCM services market." verdicts.explanation: FinThrive's own newsroom lists "FinThrive Highlights Agentic AI-Powered RCM Platform at HIMSS, Showcasing 50+ AI and Automation Use Cases Across Unified Fusion Architecture," dated March 9, 2026 (HIMSS26, Las Vegas, March 9-13, 2026), also distributed via PR Newswire. The unified 'Fusion' architecture matches FinThrive Fusion, its RCM data-intelligence platform introduced June 23, 2025.

verdicts.explanation: Infinx's own materials state it was founded in 2012 ("We launched our revenue cycle management company in 2012 in San Jose, California"; Business Wire boilerplate: "Co-founded in 2012 by Sandeep Tandon and Jaideep Tandon") and it describes itself as delivering patient access and revenue cycle solutions. verdicts.quote: an Everest Group RCM Operations PEAK Matrix "Leader" (since 2017)
verdicts.explanation: Omega's June 17, 2026 PR Newswire release (named a Leader and the only Star Performer in the Everest Group RCM Intelligent Operations PEAK Matrix Assessment 2026) explicitly states the company has maintained its position as a "Leader" in the evaluation since 2017; the first recognition was the Everest Group Healthcare Provider BPO PEAK Matrix 2017 (announced Feb 2018), the assessment later renamed RCM Operations / RCM Intelligent Operations. Minor naming nuance only.

verdicts.quote: expanded its Microsoft partnership (July 2025) to roll out 20+ generative/agentic AI solutions
verdicts.explanation: Confirmed by Omega Healthcare's July 14, 2025 PR Newswire release, "Omega Healthcare Expands Collaboration with Microsoft to Accelerate Generative and Agentic AI Capabilities, Leading RCM Innovation — Launches 20+ Generative and Agentic AI Solutions," and by independent coverage (TechTarget, July 15, 2025; HIT Consultant, July 14, 2025) describing 20+ generative/agentic AI solutions built on Azure AI Foundry and Omega's Omega Digital Platform.

verdicts.quote: Coronis (formerly Visionary RCM)
verdicts.explanation: Visionary RCM did not become Coronis. In September 2020, Visionary RCM combined with TrustHCS, T-System, and RevCycle+ under Carlyle Group majority ownership to form CorroHealth (HIT Consultant, Sept 30, 2020). Coronis Health is a separate RCM company — founded 2015, headquartered in Sykesville, Maryland — that merged with MiraMed Global Services in a Veritas Capital-backed combination (2021); its About page makes no reference to Visionary RCM. The report appears to have confused CorroHealth with Coronis Health.
verdicts.correction: The RCM BPO formerly built around Visionary RCM is CorroHealth: in September 2020, Visionary RCM merged with TrustHCS, T-System, and RevCycle+ to form CorroHealth (Carlyle-backed). Coronis Health is a different RCM firm (founded 2015, Sykesville, MD) that combined with MiraMed Global Services under Veritas Capital in 2021. Replace "Coronis (formerly Visionary RCM)" with "CorroHealth (formed in 2020 from Visionary RCM, TrustHCS, T-System, and RevCycle+)".

verdicts.quote: a single ~\$6B AI-native RCM company with ~\$800M revenue, 200+ clients / 60+ health systems
verdicts.explanation: Smarter Technologies was formed May 19, 2025 by New Mountain Capital combining SmarterDx, Thoughtful.ai, and Access Healthcare (Business Wire). The official launch release states it serves more than 200 clients, including more than 60 hospitals and health systems and 500,000+ providers, processes 400M+ transactions, and manages over $200 billion in combined revenue annually (Healthcare Innovation quoting the release).
